title: Arginine Treatment of Acute Chest Syndrome (Pneumonia) in Sickle Cell Disease Patients
brief_summary: This is a study to determine if oral arginine will increase nitric oxide in sickle cell disease (SCD) patients with acute chest syndrome (ACS). It will also assess the effects of arginine in the body and how the body uses nitric oxide in ACS.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion criteria:

* Diagnosis of sickle cell disease (Hb SS, SC, or Sbeta thalassemia)

Acute chest syndrome with the following:

* New pulmonary infiltrate on chest radiography involving a full segment of the lung and 1 of the following:
* Fever
* Cough, tachypnea, retractions, rales, or wheezing
* Chest pain

Exclusion criteria:

* Inability to take or tolerate oral medications
* Hepatic dysfunction (SGPT greater than 2 times normal)
* Renal dysfunction (creatinine greater than 2 times normal)
* Mental status or neurological changes
* Allergy to arginine
* History of priapism
* Pregnancy
